preamble: Devoicing of the voiced alveolar sibilant [z] to [s] is a widespread merger. In Chinese, the Middle Chinese voiced fricative initial 邪 *z- devoiced to s- in Mandarin. The former voicing survives as a tonal register difference: voiced initials gave the yang (lower-register) tones when the yin/yang split occurred. In Spanish, the Old Spanish voiced apico-alveolar /z̺/, spelled with a single intervocalic s as in casa, lost its voicing in the 16th century and merged with /s̺/. Tone was not involved in that change.

examples.from: Middle Chinese 寺 ziH (邪 initial) 'temple'
examples.note: The voiced initial z- devoiced to s-. The departing-tone syllable joins the Mandarin falling tone, as all departing-tone syllables do.

examples.from: Middle Chinese 俗 zjowk (邪 initial, entering tone) 'custom, vulgar'
examples.note: The voiced initial z- devoiced to s-, and the syllable now carries the yang-register rising tone (yangping).
In the 16th century the three voiced sibilants lost their voicing and merged with the voiceless ones; the apico-alveolar /z̺/ became /s̺/. Portuguese casa [ˈkazɐ] keeps the older voiced sibilant.

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2025). History of the Spanish language: Sibilants. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Spanish_language
